newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq urges food summit to end embargo - paper.
newsitem.headline: Iraq urges food summit to end embargo - paper.

text.p: An official Iraqi newspaper on Thursday urged the U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit in Rome to end stringent U.N. sanctions imposed after Baghdad's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

"Rome Summit is urged to stop the embargo crime on Iraq and announce clearly that such crime violates international norms and laws...It also contradicts the theme of the summit," the official al-Qadissiya newspaper said in an editorial.
"...the World Food Summit should end all embargoes which are being imposed by the U.S. against nations in order to dominate them," the paper said.

Iraq's vice-president Taha Mohieddin Ma'rouf is attending the summit which opened on Wednesday at the headquarters of the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO), to attempt to push forward a stalled oil-for-food deal with the U.N.
Baghdad signed an agreement with the United Nations in May allowing it to sell $2 billion worth of oil every six months to buy food and medicine.
The pact was about to be implemented in September but was halted when Baghdad sent in troops to northern Iraq to help one Kurdish faction to fight against another.
Head of the United Nations Children's Fund, UNICEF, who is attending the summit, said low fuel and food supplies meant Iraq faced a hard winter.

"What we know is that we're coming into winter (and) given fuel supplies, given food supplies, given available resources, it is going to probably be the toughest winter they've gone through so far," Carol Bellamy, UNICEF's executive director, told Reuters in an interview on Wednesday.
